what_its_for: Tetrabenazine is used to treat chorea — the involuntary, unpredictable jerking or writhing movements — caused by Huntington's disease. It works by reducing certain chemicals in the brain that cause these uncontrolled movements.
how_to_take: Take tetrabenazine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep it working steadily. Never stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can make your condition worse.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose, usually 12.5 mg once daily, and slowly increase it over several weeks until your movements are better controlled. Most people end up taking it two or three times a day. The maximum dose depends on whether you are also taking certain other medications. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tetrabenazine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past its expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking tetrabenazine — it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and make side effects worse. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, because it can cause significant drowsiness and slow your reaction time. Avoid taking reserpine or MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or selegiline) with this medication, as dangerous interactions can occur. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take before starting tetrabenazine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide, self-harm, or feelings of hopelessness; new or worsening depression or anxiety; signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, fast or irregular heartbeat, heavy sweating); unusual muscle stiffness or rigidity; difficulty swallowing or breathing; irregular heartbeat or fainting; or a high fever with no known cause. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually tired, sedated, or have trouble with balance and falling.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your involuntary movements within a few days to a couple of weeks, but it may take several weeks of dose adjustments to see the full benefit. Be patient and keep taking the medication as directed. Do not stop taking it without speaking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution — older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like drowsiness, dizziness, and falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of tetrabenazine in pregnancy is not well established, so the risks and benefits must be carefully discussed with your doctor. Liver problems: Tetrabenazine is not recommended if you have liver disease, as the body cannot process it safely. Depression and mental health: This medication can worsen depression and increase the risk of suicidal thoughts — patients with a history of depression or suicidal behavior require close monitoring. A genetic blood test (CYP2D6 testing) may be done by your doctor to determine how your body breaks down this medication, which helps guide your dosing.
